name: Banh beo
summary: Banh beo is a set of small steamed rice cakes in little dishes, topped with shrimp and eaten with a sweet-salty dip. In Da Nang the order is often bèo, nậm, and lọc together.
origin: Hue steamed cakes, eaten all along the coast. Da Nang shops sell the set as a snack or a light lunch.
howToEat: Spoon a little dip into each cup, then eat the cake from the dish. A fork flattens it.
Order the set if the sign says bèo nậm lọc. The three cakes are different textures of the same snack.
Afternoon is the easy hour. It is not a beach dinner.

The Da Nang cup is a flat white rice-flour cake. The filling is peeled shrimp pounded with ground pork, fried until browned, then fried with scallion fat. Spoon on fish sauce with chili and crushed roasted peanuts.
In Hue, a few drops of slightly sweetened fish sauce go on the cake, then you eat it from the dish.

In Dong Hoi the cake is soft, smells of new rice, and carries browned shrimp with a salty-sweet fish sauce, and it is not the small cup used in Hue and Da Nang. Another account pours it thin, with some chew, tops it with stir-fried sea shrimp, and eats it with tương ớt.
where: Bà Bé is at 100 Hoàng Văn Thụ. Order the bèo nậm lọc set.
In Hue, start at Dong Ba market, then look for bánh bèo and bánh khoái.

In Hoi An, the Hoi An World Heritage conservation centre’s 30 October 2024 note puts the cake in small bowls with a shrimp-and-pork topping and a fish sauce with a lot of chili. Its 4 September 2024 article, republishing Dân Việt, adds dried shrimp, fish cake, peanuts, and crisp pork crackling, with a sweet-sour dip. A house number and the hour are Check on arrival.
In Dong Hoi the cake is on Lê Thành Đồng, Cô Tám, and Đồng Hải.
priceBand: A snack plate, cheaper than a noodle lunch.
seoTitle: Banh beo — steamed rice cakes in Da Nang
seoDescription: Banh beo nam loc are small steamed rice cakes eaten with a spoon of dip. In Da Nang, Ba Be serves the set at 100 Hoang Van Thu in the afternoon.
